advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the recent-creates journal/probe to ticket-type creates (exclude identity) or key matches on ticket_type so identity names cannot false-match ticket titles.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:298 `return create_core("identity", name, ...)` — identity creates reach create_core

src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:281 `dup_warning = duplicate_create_warning(tracker, ticket_id=ticket_id, alias=alias or None, title=title, ...)` runs unconditionally for every create_core call including identities
recent_creates.py:128 `matches = [e for e in entries if title_norm and e["title_norm"] == title_norm]` — journal entry carries no ticket_type, so identity-name and ticket-title entries are conflated
recent_creates.py:184-185 the emitted advisory suggests `rebar link {new_ref} {cand_ref} duplicates`, a relation nonsensical for identity entities
advisory.finding: Identity creates flow through create_core, so create_identity_core now records identity entries in the shared recent-creates.json journal and runs the duplicate probe; a subsequent ticket whose normalized title matches a recently-created identity NAME (within 600s) emits a 'possible duplicate' advisory recommending `rebar link <new> <identity> duplicates` across incompatible entity types (identities are gate-/graph-exempt). The eac3 precision measurement was on same-title ticket duplicates, not identity names.
scenarios: An identity named 'Land the release' is created, then a task titled 'land the release' is created within 600s — the task create warns and suggests linking it as a duplicate of the identity
advisory.suggested_fix: Skip journal recording/probing for ticket_type=='identity' (or record ticket_type in each entry and require it to match before treating an entry as a candidate).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the concurrency test to assert exactly one WARNED and one SILENT outcome, not just that WARNED is present.
evidence: tests/unit/test_create_duplicate_warning.py:245 `assert "WARNED" in outcomes, f"neither create observed the other: {outcomes}"` — checks presence of WARNED only
The docstring at test:231 promises 'whichever runs second sees the first's entry', implying the expected outcome is exactly one WARNED and one SILENT
advisory.finding: The concurrency regression test asserts only that at least one of the two racing creates WARNED, never that the other is SILENT, so it would still pass if a serialization bug caused BOTH to warn (or both to miss but one spuriously warn).
scenarios: A future change that double-appends an entry so both racers observe a match would leave this test green

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the concurrency test force real contention (e.g. a shared start barrier via a marker file or os.pipe both children block on) so it fails if the journal flock is removed.
evidence: The two processes are launched in a plain comprehension with no barrier/pipe/event to force concurrency: `procs = [subprocess.Popen([...]) for _ in range(2)]`
Docstring claims the contract: `Two processes creating the same title at once must not both miss: the journal RMW is one flock-held critical section, so whichever runs second sees the first's entry.`

Assertion only requires `assert "WARNED" in outcomes` — satisfied whenever process 2 starts after process 1 has appended, which is the common (uncontended) ordering, so removing the flock in recent_creates.py (_journal_lock at src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:60) would not fail this test.

ABSENCE: no mechanism (marker file, os.pipe, threading.Barrier equivalent across processes) makes both processes reach _probe_and_record's read-before-append window simultaneously; the serialization/clobber contract the diff introduces is therefore regression-blind.
advisory.finding: The concurrency test forces no temporal overlap between the two subprocesses, so it does not exercise the flock serialization contract it claims to verify — it passes even if the exclusive lock is removed.
scenarios: A future change drops or narrows the exclusive flock, allowing two concurrent creates to both read an empty/pre-append journal and both miss the duplicate — this test still passes.
